title: verify_schema_baseline reports drift: 2 tenant schemas missing Postgres schema objects (tenant_277f51cc..., tenant_a319e29d...)
scope: Local/shared db (bpm_dev) tenant schema state only. Discovered as a byproduct of re-running zig build test-env-verify (checks C3/C4) while validating the ISS-0138 python3->python fix; unrelated to that fix.
symptom: `python tools/verify_schema_baseline.py --check-tenants` reports: '[FAIL] check_tenant_schemas_consistent: missing Postgres schemas for 2 tenant(s): 277f51cc-6878-445c-b010-ec648fcf95fc -> tenant_277f51cc6878445cb010ec648fcf95fc, a319e29d-ca2a-4255-bc52-aa2d987f2649 -> tenant_a319e29dca2a4255bc52aa2d987f2649'. This keeps `zig build test-env-verify` checks C3 and C4 failing, so the gate cannot report HEALTHY until resolved.
root_cause_analysis: Confirmed root cause (not the original hypothesis): src/db/provisioning.zig::provisionTenantSchema() writes the public.tenant row (storage_mode='SCHEMA', Step 6a: the ISS-0114/GH-377 promotion INSERT) in a SEPARATE statement AFTER bpm_provision_tenant_schema() creates the Postgres schema and registers it in public.tenant_schemas (Step 4). Confirmed via direct inspection of bpm_test (db_test, port 5434 -- the database zig build test-env-verify actually targets via BPM_TEST_DB_URL; the issue's reported bpm_dev/5442 reproduction command was almost certainly a stale value from the reporting session's shell, not the true locus): the two named tenant IDs had a public.tenant row with storage_mode='SCHEMA' but NO corresponding public.tenant_schemas row and no Postgres schema at all -- proof that Step 4 (schema creation + registration) never completed for these two IDs, yet Step 6a's INSERT landed anyway. 59 total SCHEMA-mode tenant rows were found, all auto-provisioned fixtures (slug pattern 'tenant-<uuid>', tenant_type='production') created within a single 4-minute window on 2026-08-05 -- consistent with concurrent integration test binaries racing tenant provisioning against tools/clean_test_db.py's cleanup sweep (same class as ISS-0106/GH-364's documented cross-binary concurrency issues), not a fresh bug introduced by any single test. tools/clean_test_db.py already deletes tenant_type='production' rows, but only by tenant_type/slug -- it had no rule that specifically targets a SCHEMA-mode row with no tenant_schemas registration, so any row left in this exact half-provisioned state survives every cleanup pass indefinitely.
resolution: 1) Reconciled the current db_test database: removed the 2 orphaned public.tenant rows directly (safe -- verified no tenant_schemas row and no Postgres schema existed for either). 2) Hardened tools/clean_test_db.py with a new sweep: DELETE FROM public.tenant WHERE storage_mode='SCHEMA' AND slug != 'default' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.tenant_schemas WHERE tenant_id = tenant.id) -- this is a safe, narrow, self-healing rule that will catch any future recurrence of this exact half-provisioned state on the next `python tools/clean_test_db.py` run, without needing a fix to the underlying provisioning-vs-cleanup race itself (which is a larger concurrency undertaking, tracked separately if it recurs). Full concurrency root-cause fix (making provisionTenantSchema's Step 4 and Step 6a atomic, e.g. via a single transaction) was assessed as out of scope for a MINOR data-hygiene issue and not attempted here.
acceptance_criteria: Either the 2 tenant schemas are provisioned (tools/verify_schema_baseline.py --auto-fix or equivalent), or the orphaned tenant registry rows are removed if the tenants are stale -- DONE (rows removed)
python tools/verify_schema_baseline.py --check-tenants reports no drift -- DONE, verified: '[OK] check_tenant_schemas_consistent: all SCHEMA-mode tenants have a Postgres schema'

zig build test-env-verify C3/C4 pass (assuming other checks are independently healthy) -- DONE, both C3 and C4 report PASS after this fix + the C3 false-positive fix in tools/verify_test_env.py (see below)
incidental_findings: tools/verify_test_env.py's C3 check used a bare substring match for 'error'/'failed'/'already exists' against the full zig build migrate output. Migration filenames 081_iss101_timers_failed_status.sql and 092_iss303_timer_fire_error_count.sql legitimately contain 'failed'/'error' in their own names, so every clean 'info:   skip  <filename>' log line for these two files tripped a permanent false BLOCKER on C3, independent of this issue's actual fix. Fixed in the same commit per the 'fix the detector's condition, not weaken it' anti-pattern rule -- see docs/anti-patterns.md's 'Satisfying a pipeline gate' entry. C3 now only matches genuine std.log error:/warning: line prefixes or a real 'already exists' DB error line.
